question.text: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mi>t</mi></mfenced></math> denotes the greatest integer <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi></math>, then number of points, at which the function <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mfenced open="|" close="|"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>+</mo></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is not differentiable in the open interval <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>, is ______.

solution.text:
Given,

fx=42x+3+9x+12-12x+20

x∈-20,20

Now we know that x is non-differentiable when x∈I

So, 12x+20 is not differentiable at x=I∈-19,-18,…0,…19=39

Now  9x+12 is not differentiable when x=I+12

So, here also total non-differentiable points are 39

Now checking modulus function

We know that modulus function are non-differentiable at point where modulus function is zero,

So at x=-32 modulus function is zero

Also fx  at x=-32 is not continuous and non-differentiable,

So, number of point of non-differentiability=39+39+1=79
